materialAtlas.creation: Built-in ImageGen, generated from the two user-supplied store references; original product photographs remain the instrument texture sources.
materialAtlas.prompt: Create a high-resolution 2048x2048 square photographic material-texture atlas for a physically rendered 3D reconstruction of this exact music store. Reference images show the store whose materials must be matched. EXACTLY FOUR equal square quadrants, edge to edge, no gutters, no labels or text. Top-left: a straight-on flat scan of the store's warm off-white painted plaster, extremely subtle hand-troweled uneven relief and tiny paint chips, no large cracks, realistic fine shallow texture, nearly uniform off-white. Top-right: a straight-on flat scan of a SINGLE white acoustic drop-ceiling panel with its characteristic tiny dark irregular holes and fissures; NO panel grid or border. Bottom-left: a straight-on flat scan of the unfinished light pine wood hanger rail, horizontal natural grain, a couple small natural knots, pale raw honey wood, no screws/hangers. Bottom-right: a straight-on flat scan of the worn grey-brown laminate floor, subtle fine grain running vertically, NO plank seams. Each quadrant seamless-looking, neutral diffuse albedo, even soft light with NO lighting gradient, NO directional shadows, NO highlights, NO perspective, NO objects. Preserve restrained real colors from store. These are photo texture samples, NOT a room rendering, NOT a design mockup, NOT an illustration. Extremely realistic fine material detail. Each quadrant fills precisely 50% width/height.
materialAtlas.limitations: Reference-matched material reconstruction, not a measured scan. Classical guitar front uses real spruce detail photography because the catalog has no full front view. Repeated display instances share four actual catalog identities, prices, and stock records.
